name: Kāpiti Coast

what_where.fact: A chain of coastal towns and beaches along State Highway 1 and the Kāpiti rail line, 40-70 km north of Wellington CBD, from Paekākāriki in the south to Ōtaki in the north (northernmost point of the Wellington Region), facing Kāpiti Island 5 km offshore. District's settlements: Ōtaki, Te Horo, Waikanae, Paraparaumu, Raumati, Paekākāriki; Paraparaumu is the most populous and the commercial centre. Wikivoyage describes it as running 'from Paekakariki to Otaki', between mountains and sea.

destination_facts.name: Kāpiti Coast (Wikipedia district article 'Kāpiti Coast District'; Wikivoyage 'Kapiti Coast'). Id kapiti-coast.
destination_facts.category_note: Coast of beaches and small towns, headlined by an island reserve. 'island' would mislead (the island is one spot); 'beach' is the best fit from the allowed list.

coordinates_recommended.reason: Between Paraparaumu town and Paraparaumu Beach (the ferry hub and Kāpiti Island departure; Wikipedia Paraparaumu -40.914,175.006; Paraparaumu Beach -40.894,174.979). Do not use Wikivoyage's region point (-40.86,175.12) or the placement.json midpoint (-40.88,175.03): both fall inland. Wikivoyage's own region page also swaps coordinates (lists Otaki at -40.983,174.954, which is Paekākāriki).

span_check.note: Farthest spot is Ōtaki at ~19 km, so 30 km would suffice for the 75% rule; 40 km is recommended so the whole Paekākāriki-Ōtaki strip (~30 km N-S) and Kāpiti Island sit on screen. The 60 km in placement.json is wider than needed.

destination_facts.rank_reason: COVERAGE.md table: 4 = 'worth a detour if you are nearby'. One headline attraction (Kāpiti Island) plus a strip of beach towns; WellingtonNZ treats it as a day-trip region; nothing at the 2-3 tier. Not 5: Kāpiti Island and the Escarpment Track draw visitors on purpose.

description_facts: Stretches from Paekākāriki to Ōtaki; unspoilt beaches, rivers, villages (Wikivoyage) https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Kapiti_Coast
Wellington to Paraparaumu is 54 minutes by Kapiti Line train; line terminates at Waikanae; 40-90 min drive from Wellington/Palmerston North https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Paraparaumu
Kāpiti Island is 10 km long, ~2 km wide, 19.65 km2, predator-free; district named after it https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kapiti_Island
Queen Elizabeth Park holds the last area of natural dunes on the Kāpiti Coast https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Elizabeth_Park,_K%C4%81piti_Coast
Ōtaki has outlet shopping on SH1 and Māori cultural heritage (Rangiātea church rebuilt 2003) https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Otaki
Coast35 is a sealed shared trail connecting Paekākāriki and Ōtaki https://www.wellingtonnz.com/visit/kapiti-coast

goodToKnow_candidate.tip: Kāpiti Island has no private landings: you must go with an authorised operator, boats leave from the Kapiti Boating Club at Paraparaumu Beach, trips depend on the weather (confirm on the morning), bags are inspected for pests before boarding, and summer bookings need to be made well in advance. Day-trip price from the operator includes the DOC permit.
goodToKnow_candidate.also: Operator's homepage showed 'Ferry Status: CANCELLED 17/10/26' when loaded, a live example of weather cancellations. Boulder Bank Loop is closed Oct-Mar for nesting seabirds (DOC): https://www.doc.govt.nz/kapiti-walks

goodToKnow_candidate.tip: The Escarpment Track is steep (about 1,200 steps, two swing bridges), is not recommended for anyone with vertigo or low fitness, has no facilities, and is easiest as a one-way walk with the train back from the other end (stations at both ends).

Queen Elizabeth Park is always open on foot, but vehicle gates shut at 6pm (1 Apr-30 Sep) or 9pm (1 Oct-31 Mar); the Wellington Tramway Museum runs trams only at weekends (Wikivoyage: Sat-Sun 11-4:30, 2016 listing, unverified).

goodToKnow_candidate.tip_alternate: Trains: Metlink Kapiti Line runs Wellington-Paraparaumu in 54 min, terminates at Waikanae, so Ōtaki and Ngā Manu need a car or bus; local buses link Paraparaumu, the beaches and Waikanae.

best_months.basis: Southern-hemisphere summer. Travel-guide climate summary: Jan-Feb warmest (~17 C mean, highs ~19-24 C depending on source), winter wettest and cooler; Wikivoyage/other sources call summer the beach season. DOC says Kāpiti Island is busy in summer. Weak caveat: the Boulder Bank track on the island is closed Oct-Mar (a minor trade-off).
best_months.confidence: medium: climate numbers came from a web-search summary of kupi.com and travel sites that disagree on highs; no NIWA/Wikipedia climate table loaded

seasonal_pattern.real_pattern: Summer demand for Kāpiti Island crossings ('bookings for the popular summer season need to be made well in advance', DOC). The operator runs a Christmas Deluxe Day Tour 26 Dec 2026-3 Jan 2027 and the Waiorua coastline loop is off-season only (Apr-Sep).
seasonal_pattern.recommendation: No seasonalTags needed; mention in bestTimeBlurb only.

destination_facts.overlap_check: Kāpiti Coast centre is ~45-55 km from Wellington CBD centre; placement.json says outside Wellington span. Mention for the owner: Staglands (Akatarawa Valley) is reached more easily from Upper Hutt (see spots).

spots.name: Kāpiti Island
bio_facts: Predator-free nature reserve 5 km (Wikipedia says 5.6 km) off the coast, 10 km long, 19.65 km2; kākā, kōkako, takahē, hihi and kiwi live wild
Access only with authorised tourism operators; private boats cannot land; boats depart from Kapiti Boating Club, 1 Manly Road, Paraparaumu Beach

Two public areas: Rangatira (east shore) and the northern end; summit Tuteremoana 521 m via Wilkinson Track (2 hr one way); Rangatira has the oldest building associated with nature conservation in NZ; overnight stays not allowed in the reserve (the operator offers private-land accommodation)
spots.bio_suggestion: A predator-free island sanctuary off Paraparaumu Beach, reached only by licensed boat, where kākā, hihi and kiwi live wild and a 2-hour track climbs to a 521 m summit.
spots.hours: Daytime tours only; operator day trip departures from 8am; about 5.5 hours on the island (Rangatira) or 4.5 hours (Waiorua/north end). Weather dependent.

visitHours.basis: Operator: 5.5 h on island plus ferry (~15-20 min each way per Wikivoyage/WellingtonNZ)

cost.basis: Operator 'from' prices per adult: Waiorua half-day from $139, Rangatira day trip from $169 (includes return ferry, DOC permit and intro talk). Guided lunch tour and overnight cost more (not recorded).

spots.name: Queen Elizabeth Park
bio_facts: Greater Wellington regional park between Paekākāriki and Raumati South, containing the last area of natural dunes on the Kāpiti Coast

Tracks around wetlands, dunes and the only kahikatea forest remnant on the coast (Te Ara o Tipapa wetland walk 45 min; Coastal Track 1 hr 20 min); US Marines WWII camp memorial; Wellington Tramway Museum (Mackays Crossing entrance); campground; horse riding and cycling
spots.bio_suggestion: A regional park of dunes, restored wetlands and coastal tracks between Paekākāriki and Raumati, with a WWII US Marines memorial and the Wellington Tramway Museum.
spots.hours: Open to foot traffic always; vehicle gates 6am–6pm (1 Apr–30 Sep) and 6am–9pm (1 Oct–31 Mar) per Greater Wellington. Tramway Museum trams Sat–Sun 11–4:30 (Wikivoyage 2016, council says same) unverified.

spots.name: Ngā Manu Nature Reserve
bio_facts: 14-hectare charitable-trust reserve in Waikanae, opened to the public in 1981; one of the largest remnants of coastal lowland swamp forest on the Kāpiti Coast

spots.bio_suggestion: A 14-hectare bird reserve in Waikanae with aviaries, a nocturnal house with kiwi and tuatara, eel feeding and a bush walk through one of the coast's last swamp forest remnants.
